correctness.rationale: All quantifiers, boundaries, and definitions checked. Girth makes every (k+1)-set a forest, hence full dual skeleton. For every connected k-set, removal of an internal tree vertex gives a codimension-one private face: any other connection creates a cycle on at most k+1 vertices. The private rows yield an integral unit diagonal, split injectivity and free homology. Standard combinatorial Alexander duality followed by simple connectivity, Hurewicz and Whitehead establishes the exact wedge. Complete verifier checked 23 finite pairs, including a noncactus theta graph and the Heawood graph; these are corroborating computations, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A parameter-uniform homotopy theorem for arbitrary high-girth graphs and unbounded k, answering a topological part of Chandrakar’s motivated higher-cut hexagonal-grid direction; includes graphs with overlapping long cycles. The private-face lemma closes the previously unresolved additional homology degree, while k=4 yields a natural local degree formula and nontrivial examples. Not just a renaming of Euler characteristic or a single computational table.
